citations.quote: MANILA, Philippines (First published Sept. 15, 8 p.m.) — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Tuesday claimed that former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque's asylum bid in Austria had been denied, a claim Roque later disputed.
The statement was made after Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Roque’s asylum application in Austria had been denied.
MANILA, Philippines — Ibinasura ang hirit na asylum ni dating presidential spokesman Harry Roque, ayon kay Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla.
“By the way, tapos na ’yung asylum, na-deny ’yung asylum ni Harry Roque. Tapos na ’yung five months. Kung may red notice na, kukunin ko siya,” pahayag ni Remulla.
Matatandaan na noong Nobyembre 2025, kinumpirma ni Roque na nag-apply siya ng asylum sa Netherlands, ngunit ipinasa ang kanyang aplikasyon sa Austria dahil dito siya nabigyan ng visa.

components.review_reason: Multiple passages explicitly state that Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla announced or claimed that Austria (or, more generally, Roque's asylum application in Austria) had been denied. Passage 1 states Remulla claimed Roque's asylum bid in Austria was denied. Passage 4 says Remulla said Roque’s asylum application in Austria had been denied. Passage 3 (in Filipino) quotes Remulla as saying Roque's asylum bid was denied, and passage 8 provides a direct quote from Remulla about the denial. Passage 9 clarifies the application was transferred to Austria. These passages together support the assertion that Remulla announced Austria did not accept Roque's asylum application. The qualifiers (Remulla as the announcer, Austria as the country, and Roque as the applicant) are preserved. There is no cited passage that contradicts the fact that Remulla made this announcement, even though Roque disputes the truth of the denial.
